new_results.statement: If u_0=sqrt(h)r, u_i=t_i r+p_i, sum p_i p_i^T=I_2, and ||p_i||^2<1/4, then some original-coordinate leaf split I,J satisfies det(S_I)det(G_J)>(27/3125)(1-h).
Using account02/B10's factorization V_3=h(det M)^2 det(S_I)det(G_J), the optimal one-hub crossing packet obeys (27/3125)hD^2(1-h)<sup V_3<=hD^2(1-h).

Under the same diffuse-transverse geometry, the row-marginal-free one-hub compiler gives a continuous C_0 density with ||p_Q||_infinity<C_*[(27/3125)hD^2(1-h)]^(-1/6). In the live h>63/64 chamber, D^2(1-h)>=2^-12 implies ||p_Q||_infinity<83.216.

partner_applied.actual_inequality: V_3>(27/3125)hD^2(1-h) on the deterministic split constructed in this run

next_step: Use the order-one hub-containing bordered pair-times-triple packet before converting the third-rank phase to a leaf-only Gram. The one-hub crossing architecture is now proven to lose exactly the scale D^2(1-h), so further partition optimization cannot solve the ultra-coloop limit.
continuity_scope: The new D^2(1-h)>=2^-12 branch, and more generally every punctured diffuse-transverse state covered by the one-hub compiler, has a continuous C_0 density. No continuity claim is made for the remaining ultra-coloop branch or full target.
